title: Attempted kidnapping suspect was Meijer upskirt peeper, records show - NewsBreak
text:
By Adriana Doria ,
6 hours ago
KENTWOOD, Mich. (WOOD) — A woman’s attempt to talk a man through his supposed grief turned into an assault as the man tried to kiss her and get into her home.
Mary Raab, 66, told News 8 she was planting flowers by her mailbox when a man approached, saying his brother died and he was struggling.
“He got out and said, ‘I have had this very traumatic incident happen to me, my brother passed away and I am in deep grief and I do not know how to deal with it,'” she said. “I am thinking, well this is very weird.”
Man arrested for attempted kidnapping in Kentwood, police say From there, Raab said that man proceeded to ask her if he could use the restroom and wash his hands. She reputedly said ‘no’ and directed him to a gas station.
“I went to shake his hand and then he put his arms around me and went to kiss me on the mouth, and I turned my head away and he planted his lips between my jawbone and my neck,” Raab said. He made it kind of difficult to break out of his embrace,” Raab said.
“It is violating somebody’s space, why do you think you have the right to do that?” she added.
Police identified that man as 29-year-old John Marcus Moore and said that he struck again that same day.
A May 2026 booking photo of John Moore from the Kent County jail. The alleged assault happened sometime between 5 p.m. and 6:30 p.m. on May 12 at Raab’s home off Poinsettia Avenue SE, police said. Shortly after, police responded to Rondo Street east of Kalamazoo Avenue for a report of an attempted kidnapping . Home surveillance video shared by police shows a 14-year-old girl — blurred to protect her identity — walking down the sidewalk when a black vehicle pulls up next to the sidewalk, headed in the opposite direction. It comes to a stop and a man gets out of the driver’s side door, lunging for the teen as she walked home from school, police said.
Police say that teen was able to fight back and Moore drove off. Her acts were described as “heroic” by the Kentwood Police Department.
A screenshot of surveillance video showing the moments a man tried to kidnap a 14-year-old girl in Kentwood on May 12, 2026. (Courtesy Kentwood Police Department) “That victim absolutely saved her own life that day, she did amazing things and fought hard and made that suspect jump back in the car and take off,” Capt. Tim Wierenga with the Kentwood Police Department told News 8.
“Obviously age didn’t matter to him, he was just looking for a victim. But I am glad that I kept my head, I am glad I didn’t let him into my house,” Raab said.
This will not be the first time Moore is behind bars.
Less than a year ago, Moore was sentenced to jail and probation for accosting women in different Meijer stores.
A 2023 booking photo of John Moore from the Kent County jail. Alleged peeper caught ‘peering over stall’ in women’s bathroom at Wyoming Meijer Target 8 previously reported that Moore was discovered when a woman looked up from the toilet and spotted Moore peering down at her from the next stall over. Surveillance cameras show Moore had also recorded an upskirt video in the store’s common area, “crouching down behind the victim” to surreptitiously position his cellphone to shoot up the shopper’s dress. That happened at a Clyde Park Meijer in 2023.
Target 8 also reported that Moore walked around the Alpine Avenue Meijer telling female customers they had a spider on their back and then grabbing their behinds. Becker said three women reported Moore’s ruse and subsequent assault.
Man who peeped on, grabbed women at Meijer stores sentenced Raab told News 8 she is grateful the situation was not worse and that everyone was OK.
“I think he chose me because he saw me as a woman alone, he was definitely testing me to see how vulnerable I was and luckily I was calm enough and level-headed enough to make him go away without having anything devastating and dramatic happen,” she said.
